intended_object: A predicate saying that a maximal simplex of the Fox–Neuwirth order-complex subdivision (for a prime p) is one of the "selected" reference simplices `selectedSimplex hp σ`, meaning it lies in the image of `σ ↦ selectedSimplex hp σ`. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation (Step S5 of the "AAK route").
explanation: The body says exactly what the docstring says: `s` is selected if and only if `s = selectedSimplex hp σ` for some permutation σ of `Fin p`. Equivalently, `s` lies in the range of `selectedSimplex hp`. So the definition does what it claims. That said, it is bookkeeping inside one specific proof. The module counts the zeros of a perturbed affine reference map. Over each top cell it picks out one maximal flag, the one whose bottom rank equals its top rank and whose bars are removed in the identity order. `IsSelected` only marks these flags so that determinant signs can be summed over them. It is not a standard notion from the literature, and there is no Mathlib counterpart to compare it with or to call broader. Hence the verdict `not_a_mathematical_object`.
